symptom: `brain capture --from-json` refused a whole batch with `json: unknown field "accepts"`: --accepts, --changes and --partly-meets had no batch spelling, so a decision accepting a lint finding (or changing a requirement) could only be captured one at a time with the flag
cause: `BatchItem` (cmd/mxcli/brain/batch.go) mirrored only the text/anchor/slice/open/source flags; the three later flags were added to the single form only, and the requirement-id check lived in the command layer (`applyVerdictFlags`) where `BuildBatch` could not reach it
insight: **When a command has two input spellings (flags and a batch), every flag added to one is a gap in the other — and the dangerous fix is the one that parses the field but drops it.** Acceptances and verdicts are body lines read by regex, so a batch that accepted `accepts` without writing the line would capture the decision and leave lint reporting the finding: stubbing the write makes the batch succeed with empty bodies. The test that pins it compares the batch entry's body to the flag path's (same order: verdicts, then acceptances) and, through the CLI, the flag form of the same decision is reported 'Already queued' as the batch one. Workaround before the fix: the exact `Accepts lint `RULE` on `@El`: reason` line in `body` is read; prose is not. The BatchItem comment promised list/staged output could be fed back in — false (id/kind/date/shard are refused), so corrected rather than extended
